pinboard.title: Can Marissa Mayer, Yahoo’s Former CEO, Help Fix A.I.’s Gender Problem?  - The New York Times
pinboard.description:
Late last year, Marissa Mayer was struggling with what felt like an impossible task.

Her daughter Marielle was turning 10, and Marielle’s teacher wanted three bullet points summarizing what made her special. Mayer — the former chief executive of Yahoo and a pioneer at Google, where she was the first female engineer — likes cracking a hard problem. But she felt overwhelmed by the range and complexity of potential answers.

So Mayer asked her personal A.I. assistant, Dazzle. Within a few seconds, Dazzle delivered an answer.

“It came back and was like, your daughter is empathetic, creative and an animal lover,” Mayer said. She thought it was perfect.

pinboard.title: ‘Bold but sane’: what we learnt from Anthropic’s 240,000-word IPO filing • Financial Times
pinboard.description:
George Hammond and Ryan McMorrow:

Anthropic has unveiled its long-awaited listing prospectus, detailing over more than 300 pages how its technology could cure disease and grow the economy, provided it does not first cause “catastrophic or existential risks to humanity”. The filing puts Anthropic on track for a blockbuster listing next month. The initial public offering on Nasdaq, under the ticker ANT, will serve as a referendum on whether public market investors are sold on the visionary zeal with which Dario Amodei’s AI lab has wooed private backers. Investors will have to swallow a complex governance structure that gives ordinary shareholders almost no power, as well as extraordinary financial and societal risks. Alongside dizzying growth and $800bn in data centre spending commitments, the company’s founders urge prospective owners of the stock “not to think of your purchase in purely transactional terms”. …The S-1 provided the clearest picture yet of Anthropic’s soaring revenue, which rose from $4.6bn last year to more than $33bn in the nine months to the end of September, according to the filing and figures recently shared with investors. Revenue per head at the five-year-old group over the past year is $6.6m. But there is a significant risk underlying that rapid growth. Just five customers accounted for 25% of revenue in the first nine months of the year, while only 250 spent more than $10m on an annual basis. Anthropic also warned that its rapid growth to date “may reflect early-stage adoption”, and could stall in the months to come. Its revenue growth has slowed this year. After more than doubling between the first two quarters of 2026, revenue grew almost 50% between the second and third quarters. …To support its spending in the near term, the start-up has a cash pile of $112bn on hand. Anthropic is pushing to become profitable, focusing on using its scarce computing power more efficiently, including by using its AI model Claude to train newer models. Anthropic spent just over $2.50 on computing power and infrastructure for every $1 of revenue in the first quarter of 2025. During the second quarter of 2026, that was down to less than 50 cents.

Big gamble. When Google published its S-1 in 2004, people were astonished to discover it had been profitable for ages. This is a different bet: more like Mosaic back in the day, perhaps.
